prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
At first, the conflict looked like a fast military crisis. By September, it was starting to look more like a long test of pressure.

On February 28, 2026, the United States and Israel began air strikes on Iran. On June 14, the two sides agreed to a ceasefire understanding. Four days later, the sea blockade was lifted.

But the pause did not reset the situation.

In July, Iran attacked three merchant ships outside approved routes. The blockade restarted on July 14.

After that, the pressure spread beyond the fighting itself. A petrochemical plant stopped production, and Iranian opposition media reported that Iran had lost part of its ability to produce natural gas. The US Navy also began clearing mines in the Strait of Hormuz and found more than 100 objects believed to be mines.

Diplomacy did not break the deadlock. On August 18, President Trump said no talks with Iran were scheduled. The 60-day period for negotiations then ended without an agreement.

A private political-risk company moved its forecast for peace from September to the end of the year. On September 4, one news report said that a month-long period of quieter fighting was ending. It described the region as moving back toward a dangerous and unsustainable military stalemate.

Taken together, these signs suggest a change in the conflict. This is no longer only a contest of military attacks. It is also a test of how long shipping, energy production, and diplomacy can stay under pressure.

But the picture is mixed.

【Point One】
One number needs careful handling. Chris Wright said more than 17 million barrels passed through the strait on September 1, a war record. But official energy data show a second-quarter average of 4.9 million barrels a day, versus more than 20 million before the war. That daily figure may show a short rebound, not a return to normal. Wright’s claim is a political assessment; the key question is whether high flows continue.

【Point Two】
The June pause shows why this is hard to unwind. The blockade was lifted, but the old system did not return; after the July attacks, it came back. The Navy found more than 100 suspected mines during its clearing work, while Iranian opposition media reported gas-capacity losses. The talks deadline passed, and the political-risk company moved its peace forecast to year-end. That makes this a test of endurance and recovery, not just the next move.

point_one.reasoning: 公式統計との比較により、17百万バレルという単日の数字が戦争前の正常化を意味しない可能性を具体的に示している。高水準の輸送が継続するかを確認すべきだという解釈も加わり、Full Storyにはない実質的な価値がある。

point_two.reasoning: 停戦後の封鎖再開、機雷、ガス生産能力、交渉期限、和平予測を並べて『耐久と回復の試験』とまとめているが、これらの事実と中心的な結論はFull Storyですでに述べられている。Point独自の新しい分析や具体的示唆はほぼなく、主に要約・言い換えにとどまる。
